title: Puncturable registered attribute-based keyword search for secure cloud data sharing
content:
by Zeyang Song, Yuyan Guo, Mingming Jiang, Zhiyao Yang

Cloud data sharing requires methods that protect sensitive files while allowing authorized users to find and access them. Centralized key generation creates a risk of key escrow, while exposed user keys may compromise previously shared data. We develop a scheme that combines encrypted keyword search with selective restriction of decryption keys in a registered framework. Users generate their own secret keys, and a key curator verifies and aggregates public registration information. Owners attach descriptive keywords and tags to encrypted files. Search compares combined keyword representations, and each new index excludes users according to the owner’s current list. Users can update their keys to remove access to selected tags while retaining access to others. Protection against later key exposure requires secure erasure of earlier secret states; existing indexes are not automatically updated when the exclusion list changes. We analyze the mechanisms and compare their computational, communication, and storage costs with two related schemes. Under the tested configuration, registration and search costs remain close to the corresponding baselines, while the combined functionality adds encryption and decryption work. The scheme provides a framework for combining encrypted retrieval with selective key restriction, clarifying the associated cost trade-offs and conditions for its use.
